_metadata.description: Fundamental physical principles for materials science reasoning
_metadata.purpose: Enable LLM to reason about material behavior using first-principles understanding
_metadata.usage: Reference these principles when explaining or predicting material properties
_metadata.source: Solid state physics and materials science textbooks
_metadata.citation: Kittel, Ashcroft & Mermin, and other standard references

metallic.description: Delocalized electrons shared among all atoms

covalent.description: Localized electron sharing between specific atoms

ionic.description: Electrostatic attraction between cations and anions

close_packing.description: Atoms pack to maximize density and minimize energy
close_packing.principle: Metals prefer high packing efficiency; covalent materials sacrifice packing for directional bonds

common_examples.Fm-3m: FCC metals (Cu, Al, Au, Pt, Ni)

wyckoff_positions.description: Symmetry-equivalent atomic positions within unit cell
wyckoff_positions.importance: Determines which sites are equivalent for defect formation

formation_energy.description: Neutral-defect energy accounting; charged defects additionally require an electron-reservoir term and finite-size corrections.
formation_energy.formula: E_f = E_defect - E_perfect - Σ n_i * μ_i

components.E_defect: Total energy of system with defect
components.n_i: N_i(defect) - N_i(reference): positive for added atoms, negative for removed atoms

implications: Defects are thermodynamically inevitable at T > 0

formation.description: Remove atom from lattice site to surface/grain boundary
energy_trends: Higher cohesive energy → higher vacancy formation energy
Higher melting point → higher vacancy formation energy

migration.description: Vacancy moves by atom hopping into empty site

interactions.vacancy_vacancy: Attractive at short range, can form di-vacancies
interactions.minimum_separation: Typically > 5 Å to avoid strong interactions

hume_rothery_rules.description: Empirical rules for substitutional solid solubility

rules.name: Size factor
rules.rule: A radius difference below about 15% is an empirical indicator for extensive substitutional solubility, not a hard gate for constructing a specified dopant.

rules.name: Electronegativity
rules.effect: Large difference → compound formation instead of solid solution

rules.name: Valence
rules.rule: Same valence preferred for high solubility

strain_effects.description: Size mismatch creates local strain field
effects: Larger dopant → compressive strain on neighbors
Smaller dopant → tensile strain on neighbors

electronic_effects.isoelectronic: Same valence, no carrier change (e.g., Ge in Si)

octahedral.description: Surrounded by 6 atoms in octahedral arrangement
octahedral.fcc_position: In the conventional FCC cell: body center [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] and edge centers such as [0.5, 0, 0]; face centers are occupied host sites.
octahedral.size: Void size and distortions depend on the host lattice.

tetrahedral.description: Surrounded by 4 atoms in tetrahedral arrangement
tetrahedral.size: Compare actual host-neighbor geometry; no host-independent size ordering.

common_interstitials.H: Hydrogen can occupy interstitial sites; tetrahedral versus octahedral preference depends on the host and conditions.
common_interstitials.C: Prefers octahedral sites, causes lattice expansion
common_interstitials.N: Similar to C, important for steel hardening
common_interstitials.O: Can form oxide precipitates at high concentration

d_band_theory.principle: Adsorption strength correlates with d-band center position
mechanism: Adsorbate states hybridize with metal d-band
Higher d-band center → more antibonding states above Fermi level → stronger binding

trends.across_period: d-band center moves down (more negative) → weaker binding
trends.filling_effect: More d-electrons → lower d-band center → weaker binding

coordination_effects.mechanism: Undercoordinated atoms have narrower d-band, higher d-band center

general_rules: Small adsorbates (H) prefer high-coordination hollow sites
CO prefers top sites on late TM, hollow on early TM
OH prefers top or bridge sites
Large molecules prefer lower coordination due to steric effects
electronic_factors: Adsorbates with unpaired electrons prefer high coordination
Adsorbates with lone pairs can bind at top sites
π-bonding adsorbates (CO, NO) have complex site preferences

fcc_surfaces.(110): Rows of atoms, bridge sites along rows
fcc_surfaces.(211): Stepped surface with (111) terraces and (100) steps

surface_energy_ordering.principle: Lower surface energy → more stable → larger facets in nanoparticles

gibbs_free_energy.application: Determines phase stability and reaction spontaneity

chemical_potential.description: Energy cost to add one atom/molecule to system
chemical_potential.importance: Determines defect formation energies and equilibrium compositions

phase_stability.convex_hull: Stable phases lie on convex hull of formation energy vs composition
phase_stability.metastability: Phases above hull are metastable, may transform given kinetic pathway

diffusion_mechanisms.interstitial: Small atom jumps between interstitial sites
diffusion_mechanisms.interstitialcy: Interstitial pushes lattice atom to new interstitial site

nucleation.heterogeneous_nucleation: Lower barrier at surfaces, defects, grain boundaries

band_theory.metals: Partially filled bands, no band gap
band_theory.semiconductors: Small band gap (< 3 eV), can be doped

fermi_level.description: Highest occupied energy level at T=0

work_function.description: Energy to remove electron from surface to vacuum
work_function.importance: Affects electron transfer in catalysis and electrochemistry
